abarim.title: Abarim
abarim.note: A range of mountains east of the Dead Sea, looking across at Jericho. Mount Nebo is the peak in it that people know, because that is where Moses stood to see the land he was not going to enter. Israel camped here at the end of the wilderness years.

abdeel.title: Abdeel
abdeel.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
abdeel.note: He is in the record for one reason, to say whose father Shelemiah was. Shelemiah was one of the men Jehoiakim sent to arrest Jeremiah and Baruch after the scroll was burned, and they did not find them.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

achbor.title: Achbor
achbor.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
achbor.note: A royal official under Josiah. He is one of the men sent to the prophetess Huldah after the law scroll turned up in the temple.

ahab-2.title: Ahab
ahab-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahab-2.note: Jeremiah names him twice, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

ahikam.title: Ahikam
ahikam.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ahikam.note: A court official under Josiah. He backed the warnings of Huldah the prophetess and later protected Jeremiah from a mob that wanted him killed, and Gedaliah was his son.

ai-2.title: Ai
ai-2.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amon.title: Amon
amon.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
amon.note: The son of Manasseh. He followed his father's early idolatry and never turned back, and his own officials killed him after two years. The people executed the plotters and made his young son Josiah king.

anathoth.title: Anathoth
anathoth.note: A priestly town in Benjamin, about three miles north of Jerusalem, and Jeremiah's home. He bought a field there as a sign of hope while announcing Jerusalem's fall. The site is identified with the village of Anata.

arabia.title: Arabia
arabia.note: Paul says he went away into Arabia for a time after his conversion, and in the New Testament the word covers the region south and east of Judea.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

ararat.title: Ararat
ararat.note: Noah's ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat as the floodwaters went down. The region is in what is now eastern Turkey.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer.title: Aroer
aroer.note: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.

arpad.title: Arpad
arpad.note: A Syrian city near Hamath. Assyrian kings kept naming it to show what they could conquer, and it fell to Tiglath-pileser III after a long siege around 740 BC. Its ruins are at Tell Rifaat, north of Aleppo.

asa.title: Asa
asa.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
asa.note: King of Judah for forty-one years, and a real reformer. He removed his own grandmother as queen mother over an obscene idol and drove the male shrine prostitutes out. Early on he trusted God against a huge Cushite invasion, but late in life he hired a foreign king against northern Israel instead.

ashdod.title: Ashdod
ashdod.note: Ashdod spelled another way, one of the five chief Philistine cities, on the coast between Ekron and Gaza. The captured ark was put in its temple of Dagon, and the affliction started there.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

ashkenaz-2.title: Ashkenaz
ashkenaz-2.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

asshur.title: Asshur
asshur.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
asshur.note: Shem's son, whose name stuck to the land and empire of Assyria on the upper Tigris. Assyria became the great power of the eighth and seventh centuries BC, deported Israel's northern tribes after Samaria fell, and kept threatening Judah.

azariah.title: Azariah
azariah.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azariah.note: This is King Uzziah of Judah under his other name.

azekah.title: Azekah
azekah.note: A fortified town in Judah's Shephelah. Joshua routed five Amorite kings near it in a hailstorm. A Lachish ostracon written during Nebuchadnezzar's last campaign says the writer is watching for Lachish's signal fires but cannot see Azekah, which some read as Azekah already fallen and others as a line of sight he never had.

azriel-3.title: Azriel
azriel-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azriel-3.note: A tribal leader of Manasseh carries the name, and so does the father of an official Jehoiakim sent to arrest Jeremiah.

azur-2.title: Azur
azur-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
azur-2.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

baalis.title: Baalis
baalis.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baalis.note: King of the Ammonites when Babylon took Judah. He put Ishmael son of Nethaniah up to murdering Gedaliah, the governor Babylon had left over the people still in the land.

baasha.title: Baasha
baasha.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baasha.note: He killed Nadab, Israel's second king, and wiped out the rest of Jeroboam's family to take the northern throne. That fulfilled a prophecy against Jeroboam's line. Baasha's own violence brought the same kind of end on his house.

babel.title: Babel
babel.note: The plain in Shinar where people, still speaking one language after the flood, set out to build a city and a tower reaching to the heavens and make a name for themselves. God answered by confusing their language.

baruch.title: Baruch
baruch.about: Jeremiah's servant living at the time of Divided Monarchy
baruch.note: Jeremiah's scribe and close companion. He wrote the prophecies down as Jeremiah dictated them. King Jehoiakim cut the scroll up and burned it, and Baruch wrote it all out again.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

bel.title: Bel
bel.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
bel.note: Babylon's title for the god Marduk, which Isaiah and Jeremiah both mock as a powerless idol that will go into captivity itself when Babylon falls.

benhadad.title: Benhadad
benhadad.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
benhadad.note: The name was a royal title in Aram-Damascus, carried by at least two kings and possibly three, all of them at war with Israel. This one is the Ben-hadad of 1 Kings 15 and 20.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beth-baal-meon.title: Beth-baal-meon
beth-baal-meon.note: East of the Jordan, on the tableland Reuben was given. The text uses several forms of the name, Baal-meon and Beon among them. Later the town passed into Moabite hands.

beth-diblathaim.title: Beth-diblathaim
beth-diblathaim.note: It is one of the towns of Moab that Jeremiah's oracle condemns. Numbers 33:46 has it as Almon-diblathaim among the wilderness stops, and Ezekiel 6:14 calls it Diblah.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-gamul.title: Beth-gamul
beth-gamul.note: Jeremiah condemns this town of Moab in his oracle, and it is likely a ruin east of Dibon on the Moabite plateau.

beth-haccerem.title: Beth-haccerem
beth-haccerem.note: House of the vineyard. Jeremiah names it as a place to light a signal fire warning of invasion from the north. Under Nehemiah its ruler, Malchiah, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.

beth-shemesh.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh.note: It was a Levitical city on Judah's northern border, its name meaning house of the sun. When the Philistines sent the ark back, it came here first and was welcomed with sacrifice.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bezer-3.title: Bezer
bezer-3.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

bozrah.title: Bozrah
bozrah.note: Edom's capital, the city of the early Edomite king Jobab. The prophets kept coming back to it in their oracles against Edom. Isaiah pictures the Lord coming from Bozrah in stained garments.

buz-3.title: Buz
buz-3.note: The name means contempt. Nahor's second son carried it, and Jeremiah uses it for a people out in the desert.

canan-6.title: Canan
canan-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
canan-6.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Jeremiah names him once.

caphtor.title: Caphtor
caphtor.note: Where the Philistines came from before they settled on Canaan's coastal plain, generally taken to be Crete or somewhere near it in the Aegean.

carchemish.title: Carchemish
carchemish.note: A major city on the west bank of the Euphrates. For a long time it was a Hittite provincial capital, and later the seat of a Neo-Hittite kingdom of its own. Nebuchadnezzar crushed Pharaoh Necho's army there.

careah.title: Careah
careah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
careah.note: Johanan's father. Johanan was the commander who warned Gedaliah of the plot to kill him after Jerusalem fell, and Careah is named each time his son is.

carmel.title: Carmel
carmel.note: Elijah's contest with the prophets of Baal happened on this mountain ridge on Israel's Mediterranean coast. Fire came down from heaven when Elijah prayed, and Baal had nothing to answer with.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chemosh.title: Chemosh
chemosh.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
chemosh.note: Moab's national god. Solomon built him a shrine to please one of his foreign wives, and that is among the reasons given for the enemies God raised against Solomon late in his reign.

chimham.title: Chimham
chimham.about: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
chimham.note: The son of Barzillai, the old Gileadite who stood by David in Absalom's rebellion. David took Chimham back to Jerusalem as the reward. Property near Bethlehem seems to have carried his name for generations.

chush.title: Chush
chush.note: Cush as a land. It lay south of Egypt, roughly modern Sudan and Ethiopia, and the Old Testament keeps coming back to it as a distant, exotic country.

coniah.title: Coniah
coniah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
coniah.note: The short form of Jehoiachin that Jeremiah uses, for the king of Judah carried off to Babylon. In that prophecy he is written down as childless, meaning none of his line would rule from David's throne.

cushi.title: Cushi
cushi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
cushi.note: The name means the Cushite, and at least two men carry it. One was the father of Shelemiah, whose son was sent to fetch Baruch after Jeremiah's scroll was burned. Another is in Zephaniah's family line, a few generations below Hezekiah.

dalaiah-2.title: Dalaiah
dalaiah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
dalaiah-2.note: He told King Jehoiakim not to burn Jeremiah's scroll, and the king burned it anyway.

damascus.title: Damascus
damascus.note: A city has stood here, on a fertile plain watered by the Barada northwest of Mount Hermon, since before the patriarchs. It was the Aramean capital that fought Israel through the ninth and eighth centuries BC. Saul was converted on the road into it, and the street called Straight was a real colonnaded street whose columns have been found.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

david.title: David
david.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
david.note: The shepherd from Bethlehem who killed Goliath and became Israel's second king, ruling a kingdom bigger than any native king held before or after. Solomon was one of his sons. Nearly half the psalms carry his name, and the Tel Dan inscription, where an enemy king boasts over the house of David, put his dynasty outside the Bible as well.

dedan.title: Dedan
dedan.note: An Arabian trading people, known in the prophets for caravans and goods. Their ancestor Dedan was a son of Abraham through Keturah.

dibon.title: Dibon
dibon.note: A Moabite city Israel took and rebuilt. King Mesha names it on the Moabite Stone as one of his own building projects.

ebed-melech.title: Ebed-melech
ebed-melech.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ebed-melech.note: When officials left Jeremiah to die in a muddy cistern, this Cushite court official got him out. Through Jeremiah, God promised Ebed-melech his own life when Jerusalem fell.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

elam.title: Elam
elam.note: A kingdom east of Babylon. In the prophets it is one of the nations among which God scattered Israel. Its people turn up again at Pentecost.

elasah-2.title: Elasah
elasah-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elasah-2.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

elealeh.title: Elealeh
elealeh.note: Reuben rebuilt this town on the grazing plateau east of the Jordan for its herds. By Isaiah's and Jeremiah's time Moab had it back, and both name it in their oracles. The ruin el-Al, just northeast of Heshbon, is the site.

elishama-3.title: Elishama
elishama-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishama-3.note: The royal secretary under Jehoiakim, in whose room the officials sat when Jeremiah's scroll was read out.

elishama-4.title: Elishama
elishama-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elishama-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice across 2 Kings and Jeremiah.

elnathan.title: Elnathan
elnathan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
elnathan.note: A royal official. He went down to Egypt to bring the prophet Uriah back to be executed. Later he was one of those who begged Jehoiakim not to burn Jeremiah's scroll, and the king burned it anyway.

ephai.title: Ephai
ephai.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ephai.note: A Netophathite. After Jerusalem fell, his sons were among the commanders who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and at first accepted the government Babylon had set up. Nothing else is recorded of him.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

evil-merodach.title: Evil-merodach
evil-merodach.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
evil-merodach.note: Nebuchadnezzar's son, Amel-Marduk in Babylonian records. In his first year he let Jehoiachin out of prison and gave him a seat at the royal table for life. He lasted only about two years before he was overthrown.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gareb-2.title: Gareb
gareb-2.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

gedaliah.title: Gedaliah
gedaliah.about: Governor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gedaliah.note: After Jerusalem fell, Babylon made him governor of Judah over the poor left in the land, and he told them to settle down and submit. Ishmael, of the royal line, murdered him within months, and the rest fled to Egypt in spite of Jeremiah telling them not to go.

gedaliah-4.title: Gedaliah
gedaliah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gedaliah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

gemariah.title: Gemariah
gemariah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gemariah.note: A royal scribe, and Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll aloud from his chamber; later his son tried and failed to stop King Jehoiakim burning it.

gemariah-2.title: Gemariah
gemariah-2.about: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
gemariah-2.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a priest from the divided-kingdom years.

gibeon.title: Gibeon
gibeon.note: They tricked Joshua into a treaty by dressing as travellers from far away, the Hivites of this city northwest of Jerusalem, and so they lived but served at Israel's sanctuary. The tabernacle stood at Gibeon for years, and Solomon had his dream there. At el-Jib dozens of jar handles stamped with the name have settled where it was.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

goath.title: Goath
goath.note: The hill Gareb to Goath is how far Jeremiah's measuring line runs for the rebuilt city, and where Goath was is unknown.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

gomorrah.title: Gomorrah
gomorrah.note: Destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, and the two became shorthand for a people ripe for judgment, from Moses through Jesus and the apostles. No remains have been confirmed. It is generally placed near the southern basin of the Dead Sea.

habazaniah.title: Habazaniah
habazaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
habazaniah.note: Grandfather of Jaazaniah, the Rechabite leader Jeremiah tested with wine. Nothing else is recorded of Habazaniah himself.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hamutal.title: Hamutal
hamutal.about: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hamutal.note: She was one of Josiah's wives, and two kings of Judah were her sons, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, who both reigned after Josiah died.

hanameel.title: Hanameel
hanameel.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hanameel.note: Jeremiah's cousin. Babylon's army was round Jerusalem when Jeremiah bought Hanamel's field in Anathoth. He did it on purpose, as a sign that land would be bought and sold in Judah again.

hananeel.title: Hananeel
hananeel.note: A tower on Jerusalem's north wall. Nehemiah lists it among the stretches rebuilt, and Jeremiah and Zechariah use it as a landmark when they describe the city to come.

hananiah.title: Hananiah
hananiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hananiah.note: He broke the wooden yoke off Jeremiah's neck and announced that Babylon's hold on Judah would be gone in two years. Jeremiah came back with word that God would put an iron yoke in its place, and that Hananiah would die within the year. He died two months later.

hananiah-8.title: Hananiah
hananiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hananiah-8.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

hananiah-9.title: Hananiah
hananiah-9.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hananiah-9.note: One of 15 men called Hananiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Jeremiah.

hazor-2.title: Hazor
hazor-2.note: Jeremiah 49 pronounces judgment on the kingdoms of Hazor and says the place will be left desolate for good. It is not Joshua's Canaanite city; the name also belonged to a place in Arabia.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hezekiah.title: Hezekiah
hezekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hezekiah.note: One of Judah's few good kings. He came after Ahaz, reopened the temple, tore down the high places, and broke up the bronze serpent Moses had made once people began worshipping it. When Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC, Hezekiah prayed, Isaiah promised deliverance, and the siege broke overnight. His seal impression has been dug up near the Temple Mount, and his tunnel still runs under the city.

hillkiah.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah.note: The high priest under Josiah who found a forgotten scroll of the law while the temple was being repaired. What he found set off Judah's last great reform.

hillkiah-6.title: Hillkiah
hillkiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hillkiah-6.note: One of 7 men called Hillkiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Jeremiah.

holon-2.title: Holon
holon-2.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

horonaim.title: Horonaim
horonaim.note: A Moabite town south of the Arnon, and Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it among the towns that would fall. The name means "two hollows". Where it was is not known for sure.

hoshaiah.title: Hoshaiah
hoshaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hoshaiah.note: He is known only as the father of one of the leaders who took the survivors down to Egypt and forced Jeremiah along against his warnings.

igdaliah.title: Igdaliah
igdaliah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
igdaliah.note: "The man of God", Jeremiah calls him, and gives nothing else. His son Hanan had a room in the temple, and that room is where Jeremiah tested the Rechabites.

immer.title: Immer
immer.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
immer.note: Head of one of David's twenty-four priestly divisions, and his family name comes back with the returning exiles.

irijah.title: Irijah
irijah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
irijah.note: He was the guard captain at the Benjamin Gate who stopped Jeremiah leaving Jerusalem during a lull in the Babylonian siege and accused him of deserting to the Chaldeans. The princes had Jeremiah beaten and locked up.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

ishmael.title: Ishmael
ishmael.about: Jeremiah's adversary living at the time of Divided Monarchy
ishmael.note: After Jerusalem fell this Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor the Babylonians had set over the land, and the killing sent another wave of Jews running for Egypt.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jaazaniah.title: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jaazaniah.note: More than one man had the name. One is an army captain who came to the new governor after Jerusalem fell, in Kings and again in Jeremiah; another heads the family Jeremiah brought into the temple and offered wine.

jaazer.title: Jaazer
jaazer.note: Jazer, an Amorite town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Israel took it and gave it to Gad, then to the Levites of Merari. Isaiah and Jeremiah both use its ruined vineyards as a picture of Moab's ruin.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jahaz.title: Jahaz
jahaz.note: Moses beat Sihon, the Amorite king, at Jahaz, on the plateau north of the Arnon. The town went to Reuben and then to the Merarite Levites, and because it changed hands with Moab more than once, Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it in their oracles against Moab.

jeconiah.title: Jeconiah
jeconiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeconiah.note: Another name for Jehoiachin, the king of Judah carried off to Babylon. In the end a Babylonian king let him out and gave him a seat at the royal table.

jehoiachin.title: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiachin.note: Three months on Judah's throne, then he surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and went to Babylon with much of Jerusalem's upper class. He spent thirty-seven years a prisoner. A new Babylonian king let him out and fed him at the royal table for the rest of his life, and 2 Kings ends there.

jehoiada-5.title: Jehoiada
jehoiada-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiada-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

jehoiakim.title: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiakim.note: Pharaoh Necho put him on Judah's throne. When Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, he cut it off a section at a time and burned it in the fire pot, while his advisors begged him to stop. Jeremiah had it written out again, with more added.

jehonadab.title: Jehonadab
jehonadab.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehonadab.note: Rechab's son, who gave his family rules against wine and fixed houses, and they kept them for generations. He rode with Jehu to watch the purge of Baal worship.

jehucal.title: Jehucal
jehucal.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehucal.note: Zedekiah sent him with the priest Zephaniah to ask Jeremiah to pray during the last siege. Later he was among the officials who had Jeremiah thrown into a cistern.

jehudi.title: Jehudi
jehudi.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehudi.note: Jehoiakim sent him to fetch Jeremiah's scroll and read it aloud. It was the scroll the king then cut up and burned as he heard it.

jerahmeel-3.title: Jerahmeel
jerahmeel-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jerahmeel-3.note: One of 3 men called Jerahmeel. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Jeremiah.

jeremiah-3.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah-3.note: The prophet's namesake, and nothing more to him than a daughter: she was mother to two kings of Judah, and he is named only as her father.

jeremiah-8.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

jeremiah.title: Jeremiah
jeremiah.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jeremiah.note: A priest's son from Anathoth, called as a young man in Josiah's thirteenth year. For four decades he told Judah Babylon was coming, and for that he was jailed, dropped in a cistern, and had his scroll burned. He saw Jerusalem fall as he had said, then was dragged off to Egypt against his will. His scribe Baruch may be the Berekhyahu on a clay seal from his lifetime.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jezaniah.title: Jezaniah
jezaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jezaniah.note: Hoshaiah's son, the Maachathite, led one of the bands of Judean soldiers who got out into the countryside when Babylon besieged Jerusalem. He submitted to Gedaliah, Babylon's governor. After Gedaliah was murdered he was one of the leaders who, against Jeremiah's warning, took the people left in Judah off to Egypt.

johanan.title: Johanan
johanan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
johanan.note: He commanded troops after Jerusalem fell and warned Gedaliah, the new governor, that someone was coming to kill him. Gedaliah would not believe it, and the plot went through.

jonadab.title: Jonadab
jonadab.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonadab.note: The Rechabites' ancestor, who told his descendants never to drink wine. Generations on they were still keeping it, and Jeremiah held them up as people who obeyed a father's word.

jonathan-10.title: Jonathan
jonathan-10.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonathan-10.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

jonathan-3.title: Jonathan
jonathan-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jonathan-3.note: They made his house into a prison, and Jeremiah was locked in it. The prophet later begged the king not to send him back there to die.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

josiah.title: Josiah
josiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
josiah.note: Made king of Judah at eight after his father Amon was murdered. In his eighteenth year workmen repairing the temple found a forgotten scroll of the law, and its reading set off Judah's last great reform: pagan altars torn down, the priests of the high places killed, and a Passover like none since the judges. He died young at Megiddo, trying to stop the Egyptian army reaching Assyria.

jucal.title: Jucal
jucal.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jucal.note: One of Zedekiah's officials who had Jeremiah dropped into a cistern for weakening the defenders of Jerusalem. He belonged to the party at court that wanted to keep fighting Babylon, and earlier in the same crisis he is called Jehucal.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kedar.title: Kedar
kedar.about: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
kedar.note: Ishmael's son, and the father of a desert tribe known for dark tents and good archers. Poets use Kedar for far-off wilderness living, and the Song of Solomon uses it for dark beauty.

kerioth.title: Kerioth
kerioth.note: God's judgment on Moab, in Jeremiah and Amos, names this Moabite city. Judas Iscariot's name may mean "man of Kerioth."

kidron.title: Kidron
kidron.note: The valley along Jerusalem's east side, between the city and the Mount of Olives. Reforming kings dumped smashed idols and temple rubbish into it, and Jesus crossed it with his disciples on the way to Gethsemane the night he was arrested.

kir-haraseth.title: Kir-haraseth
kir-haraseth.note: Moab's fortress capital, modern Kerak in Jordan. When Mesha of Moab rebelled after Ahab died, Israel, Judah and Edom besieged him there, and he sacrificed his own son on the wall, which ended the siege. His own account of the revolt survives on the Moabite Stone, found in 1868.

kiriathaim.title: Kiriathaim
kiriathaim.note: It started out as a town of Reuben's and ended up in Moab, on Jeremiah's list of the cities God's judgment would fall on.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kolaiah.title: Kolaiah
kolaiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
kolaiah.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

lachish.title: Lachish
lachish.note: A heavily fortified Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands. Joshua took it, Rehoboam rebuilt it into one of Judah's strongest fortresses, and in 701 BC Sennacherib's Assyrians took it again. Assyria carved the siege on wall reliefs now in the British Museum. The ruins at Tell ed-Duweir also gave up the Lachish Letters, written during Babylon's last siege, just before Jerusalem fell.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

libnah.title: Libnah
libnah.note: A royal Canaanite city near Lachish that Joshua took and gave to the Levites in Judah. It held out against Sennacherib's Assyrians. Hamutal, Josiah's wife and mother of two of Judah's last kings, came from there.

luhith.title: Luhith
luhith.note: In Isaiah and Jeremiah, refugees climb the road up to Luhith in Moab weeping. It was somewhere between Zoar and Horonaim, exactly where is unknown.

maachathite.title: Maachathite
maachathite.note: Someone from Maacah, the small Aramean kingdom near Mount Hermon that Israel never fully brought under. Eliphelet, one of David's officers, was a Maachathite.

maaseiah.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah.note: Jeremiah names him only as the father of a priest the king sent to the prophet.

maaseiah-12.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-12.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-12.note: One of 20 men called Maaseiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Jeremiah.

maaseiah-13.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-13.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-13.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

maaseiah-3.title: Maaseiah
maaseiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
maaseiah-3.note: Two of his grandsons turn up in Jeremiah. One wrote out the deed when Jeremiah bought a field, and the other went on a journey with the king carrying one of Jeremiah's scrolls.

madai.title: Madai
madai.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
madai.note: Japheth's son, and the ancestor of the Medes, who later joined Persia in taking Babylon.

madmen.title: Madmen
madmen.note: Jeremiah names this Moabite town in his judgment on Moab and puns on it: it sounds like the Hebrew for "be silenced," and Moab would be silenced.

malchiah.title: Malchiah
malchiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
malchiah.note: Several men carried this name, many of them priests or from Levitical families. Their verses run from the lists in Chronicles through the men who rebuilt sections of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah, and on into Jeremiah.

manasseh-2.title: Manasseh
manasseh-2.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
manasseh-2.note: Hezekiah's son, who reigned in Judah longer than any king and did more harm than any. He rebuilt the high places, practiced sorcery, apparently sacrificed his own son, and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. Chronicles says captivity in Babylon broke his pride and he repented, but his reforms died with him.

mattan-2.title: Mattan
mattan-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
mattan-2.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

mephaath.title: Mephaath
mephaath.note: A Levitical city in Reuben's land, given to the Merarite Levites. By Jeremiah's time Moab held it, so it turns up in his oracle against Moab. The site east of the Jordan has not been pinned down.

merathaim.title: Merathaim
merathaim.note: "Double rebellion," Jeremiah's taunting name for a district of Babylon. It twists an Akkadian name for the marshes near the head of the Persian Gulf.

merodach.title: Merodach
merodach.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
merodach.note: Marduk, Babylon's chief god. Jeremiah announces Babylon's fall with "Merodach is broken in pieces." The Cyrus Cylinder credits Marduk with handing Babylon to Cyrus, the very fall the oracle looks for.

micah.title: Micah
micah.note: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.

micah-4.title: Micah
micah-4.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
micah-4.note: The eighth-century prophet of Judah, writing at the same time as Isaiah. His short book attacks the injustice of Israel and Judah and names Bethlehem as the birthplace of a coming ruler, a line Matthew quotes in the nativity. The name means "who is like the LORD."

migdol.title: Migdol
migdol.note: "Tower," a fortified point on Egypt's northeastern border. One Migdol is on Israel's route to the crossing of the sea. Jeremiah names a Migdol where Jewish refugees settled in Egypt, and Ezekiel's "from Migdol to Syene" means the whole length of the country.

minni.title: Minni
minni.note: A kingdom in the mountains east of Assyria, in what is now northwestern Iran, generally taken as Mannea of the Assyrian records. Jeremiah calls it out with Ararat and Ashkenaz to march on Babylon.

mitspah.title: Mitspah
mitspah.note: A watchtower name, which is why so many places carry it. This one is where Jacob and Laban piled stones and agreed to keep apart.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

molech.title: Molech
molech.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
molech.note: A god of the Canaanites and Ammonites, worshipped with the sacrifice of children. The law forbids it again and again, and still some kings did it, Ahaz and Manasseh among them.

morashthite.title: Morashthite
morashthite.note: "From Moresheth," the prophet Micah's town in the Judean lowlands near Gath. Nearly a century after Micah spoke, the elders in Jeremiah's day quoted his warning against Jerusalem, and that he went unpunished, to save Jeremiah's life.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nebo.title: Nebo
nebo.note: The mountain in Moab where Moses looked over the promised land before he died, taken as Jebel Neba on the ridge of Pisgah east of the Dead Sea. A Reubenite town nearby had the same name, and the oracles against Moab condemn it.

nebuchadnezzar.title: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar.about: Emperor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuchadnezzar.note: King of Babylon. He destroyed Jerusalem and its temple in 586 BC and carried Judah off, and the Bible still calls him the tool God used to judge his people. Daniel tells how, after boasting of his greatness, he went mad and lived like an animal for seven years, until he gave God the glory and got his throne back.

nebushazban.title: Nebushazban
nebushazban.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebushazban.note: Rab-saris, chief of the court officials, in Nebuchadnezzar's service. After Jerusalem fell he was one of the senior men sent to find Jeremiah, see he was treated well and let him out of the court of the guard. The name means something like "Nabu, save me."

nebuzaradan.title: Nebuzaradan
nebuzaradan.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nebuzaradan.note: He commanded the Babylonians who burned Jerusalem and its temple. To Jeremiah, though, he showed unusual kindness, and let the prophet choose whether to go to Babylon or stay in Judah.

necho.title: Necho
necho.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
necho.note: Necho the Second, pharaoh of Egypt, killed King Josiah at Megiddo. Afterwards he removed Josiah's son Jehoahaz and set up another son, Jehoiakim, under him.

nehelamite.title: Nehelamite
nehelamite.note: Shemaiah the Nehelamite was a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon. He wrote to the priests in Jerusalem to have Jeremiah silenced, and Jeremiah condemned him for prophesying lies. Where the name comes from is unknown; some read it as "dreamer."

nergal-sharezer.title: Nergal-sharezer
nergal-sharezer.about: Babylonian official living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nergal-sharezer.note: One of Nebuchadnezzar's officers at the fall of Jerusalem in 586 BC; a man of this name with the title Rab-mag helped get Jeremiah out of prison. Scholars generally take him for Neriglissar, who later killed his brother-in-law Evil-Merodach and ruled Babylon from about 560 to 556 BC.

nergal-sharezer-2.title: Nergal-sharezer
nergal-sharezer-2.about: Babylonian official of Samgar living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nergal-sharezer-2.note: One of Nebuchadnezzar's officers at the fall of Jerusalem. The name belongs to the Babylonian god Nergal.

neriah.title: Neriah
neriah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
neriah.note: Baruch was his son, Jeremiah's scribe, and so was a royal official, which made Neriah's a family of some weight in Judah's last years before Babylon.

nethaniah.title: Nethaniah
nethaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaniah.note: Father of Ishmael, the man of royal blood who murdered Gedaliah, the governor Babylon set over Judah after Jerusalem fell.

nethaniah-4.title: Nethaniah
nethaniah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
nethaniah-4.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

netophathite.title: Netophathite
netophathite.note: From Netophah, a small town near Bethlehem. Several of David's mighty men carried the name, and later some Levitical singers did too.

nimrim.title: Nimrim
nimrim.note: Isaiah and Jeremiah both name the waters of Nimrim, a once-fertile spot in Moab, in their oracles of judgment against that country.

no.title: No
no.note: Nahum points to the fall of No, the Hebrew name for the Egyptian city of Thebes, as a warning to Nineveh that no city is too strong for God's judgment.

noph.title: Noph
noph.note: Memphis, under its Hebrew name, which several prophets use when they speak of Egypt's coming judgment.

pashur-2.title: Pashur
pashur-2.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pashur-2.note: He had Jeremiah beaten and locked in the stocks overnight for prophesying judgment. In the morning Jeremiah gave him a new name, Magor-missabib, terror on every side.

pashur-3.title: Pashur
pashur-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pashur-3.note: One of 4 men called Pashur. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in Jeremiah.

pathros.title: Pathros
pathros.note: Upper Egypt. Jewish refugees fled there, and the prophets name it among the places God promised to gather his scattered people back from.

pekod.title: Pekod
pekod.note: Not a person. Pekod is a tribal or regional name in southern Babylonia, the Puqudu of Assyrian and Babylonian records, and both Jeremiah and Ezekiel bring it into their oracles against Babylon.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

pharaoh-8.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

pharaoh-hophra.title: Pharaoh-hophra
pharaoh-hophra.about: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
pharaoh-hophra.note: Known to history as Apries, king of Egypt from about 589 to 570 BC. He backed Zedekiah's revolt against Babylon for a while and then pulled out, and Jerusalem fell in 586 BC.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phut.title: Phut
phut.note: A son of Ham in the table of nations. The prophets tie his descendants to northern Africa, likely ancient Libya, and keep listing them among the hired soldiers in other people's armies.

rab-mag.title: Rab-mag
rab-mag.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rab-mag.note: It is a Babylonian court title, roughly chief of the magi, and not a name. Nergal-sharezer held it, one of the officials Nebuchadnezzar sent to see Jerusalem fall.

rab-saris.title: Rab-saris
rab-saris.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rab-saris.note: A court title, roughly chief officer, not a man's name, and officials holding it turn up at both sieges of Jerusalem.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

rachel.title: Rachel
rachel.about: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
rachel.note: Jacob's favourite wife. He was tricked into marrying her older sister Leah first and had to work another seven years for Rachel. For years Leah bore son after son while Rachel had none.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

rechab.title: Rechab
rechab.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rechab.note: His son Jehonadab laid down a rule his descendants kept for generations: no wine, no permanent houses. Jeremiah held the Rechabites up as a rebuke to Judah.

rechah.title: Rechah
rechah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
rechah.note: The verses filed here are Jeremiah 35, where the prophet brings the Rechabites into the temple and sets wine in front of them. They refuse it, keeping their father's command.

riblah.title: Riblah
riblah.note: Twice a wartime headquarters. The town sat on the east bank of the Orontes in the land of Hamath, where the roads between Egypt, Palestine and Babylon crossed. Pharaoh Necho used it first, and later Babylon did the same.

samaria.title: Samaria
samaria.note: Omri bought a hill from a man called Shemer and built a capital on it. Samaria took over from Tirzah as the seat of the northern kingdom. Ahab and the kings after him ruled from there.

samgar-nebo.title: Samgar-nebo
samgar-nebo.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
samgar-nebo.note: Listed with the Babylonian officers who sat down in Jerusalem's middle gate in 586 BC, once Nebuchadnezzar's army was through the wall. Whether Samgar-nebo is a name or a title is not settled.

samuel.title: Samuel
samuel.about: Prophet living at the time of United Monarchy
samuel.note: Hannah prayed for a son and gave him to the Lord before he was born. He grew up to be the last of the judges and the first great prophet. Israel's first two kings were both anointed by him.

sarsechim.title: Sarsechim
sarsechim.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
sarsechim.note: He sat in the middle gate with the other Babylonian officers after Jerusalem's walls were breached, and Jeremiah 39:3 names him once.

seraiah.title: Seraiah
seraiah.about: High Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah.note: The chief priest in Jerusalem when it fell. Nebuchadnezzar had him executed, and the name runs on through several later generations of priests.

seraiah-4.title: Seraiah
seraiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah-4.note: One of 8 men called Seraiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in 2 Kings and Jeremiah.

seraiah-5.title: Seraiah
seraiah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah-5.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Jeremiah names him twice.

seraiah-8.title: Seraiah
seraiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
seraiah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

shallum.title: Shallum
shallum.about: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
shallum.note: He is a Levite of the years after the exile, named at 1 Chronicles 9:17, 9:19 and 9:31 in the lists of those who kept the gates.

shallum-11.title: Shallum
shallum-11.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-11.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

shallum-12.title: Shallum
shallum-12.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shallum-12.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Jeremiah names him once.

sheba.title: Sheba
sheba.note: The Queen of Sheba came a long way, probably from southern Arabia. She came to test Solomon with hard questions. She went home saying the reports she had heard did not tell the half of it.

shebam.title: Shebam
shebam.note: Good grazing land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon, which Reuben and Gad asked for because of their flocks.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

shelemiah.title: Shelemiah
shelemiah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelemiah.note: The name of a gatekeeper in 1 Chronicles 26:14. In Jeremiah 37:3 and 38:1 it belongs to the father of an official the king sent to the prophet.

shelemiah-4.title: Shelemiah
shelemiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelemiah-4.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shelemiah-5.title: Shelemiah
shelemiah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelemiah-5.note: One of 8 men called Shelemiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in Jeremiah.

shelemiah-6.title: Shelemiah
shelemiah-6.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shelemiah-6.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years, and Jeremiah is the only book that names him.

shemaiah-20.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-20.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-20.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Jeremiah names him once.

shemaiah-21.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-21.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-21.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

shemaiah-4.title: Shemaiah
shemaiah-4.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shemaiah-4.note: In Jeremiah 29 he writes letters from exile against Jeremiah. The answer that comes back is that none of his line will live to see the good God has planned for the people.

shephatiah-8.title: Shephatiah
shephatiah-8.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
shephatiah-8.note: A man from the divided-kingdom years. Jeremiah names him once.

sheshach.title: Sheshach
sheshach.note: Babylon in code. Swap each Hebrew letter for the one counted from the other end of the alphabet, a cipher called atbash, and Babylon comes out as Sheshach. Jeremiah uses it in his oracles.

shihor-2.title: Shihor
shihor-2.note: A stream on Egypt's northeastern edge, used as the marker for the southwest corner of the land promised to Israel.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

solomon.title: Solomon
solomon.about: King living at the time of United Monarchy
solomon.note: David and Bathsheba's son, and Israel's third king. He was rushed onto the throne after his half-brother Adonijah tried to take it while David lay dying. Early on he asked God for wisdom.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

tahapanes.title: Tahapanes
tahapanes.note: An Egyptian fort town on the eastern edge of the Nile delta. After Gedaliah was murdered the refugees ran there and took Jeremiah with them against his advice, and he said there that Nebuchadnezzar would set his throne over stones buried at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace.

tanhumeth.title: Tanhumeth
tanhumeth.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
tanhumeth.note: A Netophathite whose son Seraiah was one of the army captains who came over to Gedaliah after Jerusalem fell.

tarshish.title: Tarshish
tarshish.note: Far to the west, at the edge of what Israel knew of the sea. Solomon's ships went there for gold, and ships of Tarshish came to mean any big ocean-going ship. Jonah boarded one at Joppa to get away from Nineveh.

tekoa.title: Tekoa
tekoa.note: It sat about six miles south of Bethlehem, on the edge of the wilderness that carries its name. Rehoboam fortified it, and Amos was a herdsman there when he was called to prophesy against Israel.

tema.title: Tema
tema.note: An oasis in the north Arabian desert, on the caravan road between Damascus and the Arabian interior, named for a son of Ishmael. Job's friend Eliphaz compares Job's useless helpers to the caravans of Tema. Much later the Babylonian king Nabonidus made it his residence.

tophet.title: Tophet
tophet.note: The place in the Valley of Hinnom where children were burned to Molech, until Josiah defiled it. Jeremiah said the valley would fill with the dead. Later Jewish pictures of Gehenna drew on it.

tyre.title: Tyre
tyre.note: The leading Phoenician port, partly on the mainland and partly on an island offshore, rich from sea trade and purple dye made from murex shells. Its king Hiram sent cedar and craftsmen for David and Solomon. The prophets attacked its pride and said it would fall.

uphaz.title: Uphaz
uphaz.note: Gold from Uphaz overlays idols in Jeremiah and belts the figure in Daniel's vision. Nobody knows where it was, and it may just be a variant of Ophir.

uriah-4.title: Uriah
uriah-4.about: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
uriah-4.note: He was a prophet who said the same things Jeremiah did and was killed for it. Jeremiah 26:20–23 is the whole of what is known.

uz.title: Uz
uz.note: Job lived in the land of Uz. Where it was is uncertain, somewhere east of Israel, perhaps in Edom.

zedekiah.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah.note: The last king of Judah. Nebuchadnezzar put him on the throne, and he rebelled anyway, against everything Jeremiah told him. Jerusalem was destroyed, he was caught running, his sons were killed in front of him, and then they blinded him.

zedekiah-3.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah-3.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah-3.note: One of 6 men called Zedekiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named twice in Jeremiah.

zedekiah-5.title: Zedekiah
zedekiah-5.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zedekiah-5.note: Jeremiah names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

zephaniah.title: Zephaniah
zephaniah.about: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
zephaniah.note: A priest, not the prophet of the book. Jeremiah's verses show him carrying messages between the king and Jeremiah, and 2 Kings 25:18 counts him among those taken when Jerusalem fell.

zimri-3.title: Zimri
zimri-3.note: Named once, in Jeremiah, and nowhere else.

zion.title: Zion
zion.note: The fortified hill on Jerusalem's southeastern ridge that David took from the Jebusites and called the city of David. He built his palace there. Archaeologists have uncovered the Stepped Stone Structure on that ridge, and many tie it to David's time.

zoar.title: Zoar
zoar.note: Lot asked that this little town be spared so he could run to it, and it was, while Sodom and Gomorrah burned. It was first called Bela, and it lay where Moab met the Dead Sea plain.
